case.title: Upgrading the runtime while the profile keeps official @deepseek-ai/dsh-* at 0.1.5-rc.3 disables the `session` row

reported.symptom: after the runtime upgrade the Web app does not come up: `dsh: startup failed: 3 required plugins did not activate`; 18 plugins wait for services (agent-loop → sessions, webserver → webStartup, connection → webRuntime, ...), and the browser shows ~22 client plugins pending
reported.runtime_trace: one stderr line per stale row: `dsh: disabling profile plugin row "session": Plugin @deepseek-ai/dsh-session@0.1.5-rc.3 is incompatible with dsh 0.2.0-rc.2: peerDependencies {...}`. The startup summary only names the symptom (`typert-loader: ... codec has no create() factory`), never the stale profile
user_hypotheses: a third-party plugin with a mismatched peer range breaks boot (ruled out by the reporter: only dsh-mobile-theme@0.5.0 installed, the UI renders with 0 console errors)
the front end is buggy (ruled out: the server exits before the browser is served)
the service did not start (it is the consequence, not the cause)
reported.root_cause: the profile still resolves official @deepseek-ai/dsh-* at 0.1.5-rc.3, whose @deepseek-ai/dsh-* peers are pinned to the 0.1.5 line; against the 0.2.0-rc.2 runtime every staled row is denied by the admission preflight
reported.fix_verified_by_reporter: reproduced in an isolated home with `DSH_HOME=<tmp> dsh plugin --profile web add @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app@0.1.5-rc.3` then `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`; the reporter offers to test a patch

deviations: the report's message elides the requirement map (`peerDependencies {...}`); the key used here (@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope) is the only @deepseek-ai/dsh* peer that dsh-session@0.1.5-rc.3 declares at all, so it is necessarily the unmet requirement behind the line quoted in the report — see plugin-dsh-session.json
only one of the stale rows (`session`) is reproduced; the report says one such line exists per stale row and leaves the others unnamed
bundles omitted: the stale bundle (@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app@0.1.5-rc.3) is modelled as a directly resolved row module, because the published bundle patch is not reproduced
the `typert-loader` codec failure and the browser-side pending list are downstream of the same denial and are not modelled

remediation.note: explicit exemption for this exact plugin version and runtime version
disable row "session" in patch:profile when @deepseek-ai/dsh-session is no longer needed
1 requirement(s) exclude 0.2.0-rc.2; either upgrade the plugin or stay on a runtime it declares
install a plugin build whose declarations include 0.2.0-rc.2 (profile: web)
an exemption bypasses the declaration only; behaviour is still unproven

hit.why: the labelled target is named and the labelled requirement is the one that failed
